newsitem.title: UK: Euro oil swaps mixed in unsettled crude market.
newsitem.headline: Euro oil swaps mixed in unsettled crude market.

text.p: European oil swaps were mixed on Monday as the whole market tried to gauge decidedly edgy screen crude.
Brent CFDs were a touch stronger for the close in contracts but weaker further out, fuel was broadly steady as was naphtha while gasoline lost $2 or so.

Brent CFDs for July 7-11 were pegged at +6/7 cents against August Brent compared with flat on Friday. July 14-18 slipped to -18 cents or so from -13 cents and July 21-25 also dropped to -20 from -15 cents. July 28 to August 1 was also easier by a few cents at -21 cents against August.
CFD trades were sparse with only July 10-11 done at -2 cents early in the day.
Heavy fuel swaps swayed higher before easing back. Dealers said July was hovering around $84.50 and $85.25 at the end of the day spent in a market characterised as quiet.

Low sulphur swaps also held around $93.75 with a physical cargo done at $94 cif NWE loading end of the month. Dealers said that if European levels eased much further then barrels would be picked up for the U.S.
"The U.S. interest is giving the market a floor," said one dealer.
Gasoline saw August sold at $185 and subsequently offered at $185 while July was bid down to $183. Traders said unleaded premium barges were sold at $183.50 and $184.25 with regular going at $178.50.
Naphtha swaps eased back about 50 cents with little heard done. "Talk is around $174/175 and swaps have been done, but privately," said one trader.
